Package org.bsc.langgraph4j.state

Interface Reducer<T>

Type Parameters:
T - the type of the values to combine
All Superinterfaces:
BiFunction<T,T,T>
All Known Implementing Classes:
AppenderChannel.ReducerAllowDuplicate, AppenderChannel.ReducerDisallowDuplicate
public interface Reducer<T> extends BiFunction<T,T,T>
Represents a binary operator that combines two values of the same type into a single value. In LangGraph4j, a Reducer is invoked by a Channel to merge a new value with the channel's current value. The first argument (old value) is the channel's current value (or its default if the channel has not been written to yet); the second argument (new value) is the value written by the current node.

Example built-in reducers:

  • AppenderChannel - appends new values to a list
  • RemoveByHash - removes a value from a list by identity comparison

Null handling: implementations must decide how to handle null values. A common pattern is to treat null as "no change" (return the old value unchanged) or to treat it as a signal to remove the channel. Consult the specific implementation's documentation.

Thread safety: a single Reducer instance may be invoked concurrently by multiple threads during parallel graph execution. Reducers should be stateless or use appropriate synchronization.
